match.title: The Sequence Alignment/Map format and SAMtools.

stewardship.abstract:
Summary

The Sequence Alignment/Map (SAM) format is a generic alignment format for storing read alignments against reference sequences, supporting short and long reads (up to 128 Mbp) produced by different sequencing platforms. It is flexible in style, compact in size, efficient in random access and is the format in which alignments from the 1000 Genomes Project are released. SAMtools implements various utilities for post-processing alignments in the SAM format, such as indexing, variant caller and alignment viewer, and thus provides universal tools for processing read alignments.

Availability

http://samtools.sourceforge.net.

Short impact summary

The Sequence Alignment/Map format and SAMtools (2009) in Bioinformatics. 68795 citations.

Full narrative

The Sequence Alignment/Map format and SAMtools (2009) in Bioinformatics is authored by Heng Li, Robert E. Handsaker and Alec Wysoker. Topics: Computer science, Search engine indexing, Sequence alignment, k-mer and Multiple sequence alignment.

68795 citations (OpenAlex). Citations peaked in 2021 with 7630 citing works. Citing venues include bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory), Nature Communications and Scientific Reports.

Limited online visibility beyond citations.
